passages.text: Meanwhile, Saul was still breathing out murderous threats against the disciples of the Lord. He approached the high priest and requested letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any men or women belonging to the Way, he could bring them as prisoners to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Saul hated the disciples of the Lord.
He threatened to kill them.
He went to the high priest.
He asked the high priest for letters.
He wanted to take these letters to the synagogues in Damascus.
He wanted permission to arrest people who followed the Way.
He wanted to find men and women who belonged to the Way.
He planned to tie them up.
He wanted to bring them as prisoners to Jerusalem.
passages.original: Ὁ Δὲ Σαῦλος ἔτι ἐμπνέων ἀπειλῆς καὶ φόνου εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς τοῦ Κυρίου προσελθὼν τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ ᾐτήσατο παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐπιστολὰς εἰς Δαμασκὸν πρὸς τὰς συναγωγάς ὅπως ἐάν τινας εὕρῃ τῆς Ὁδοῦ ὄντας ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας δεδεμένους ἀγάγῃ εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: As Saul drew near to Damascus on his journey, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.
passages.sermon:
Saul traveled toward Damascus.
He came close to the city.
Suddenly, a light shone around Saul.
This light came from heaven.
passages.original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ πορεύεσθαι ἐγένετο αὐτὸν ἐγγίζειν τῇ Δαμασκῷ ἐξαίφνης τε αὐτὸν περιήστραψεν φῶς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ

passages.text: He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?”
passages.sermon:
Saul was traveling to Damascus.
A light from heaven suddenly flashed around him.
Saul fell to the ground.
He heard a voice speak to him.
The voice said, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?”
passages.original: καὶ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἤκουσεν φωνὴν λέγουσαν αὐτῷ Σαοὺλ Σαούλ τί με διώκεις

passages.text: “Who are You, Lord?” Saul asked. “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,” He replied.
passages.sermon:
Saul spoke.
He said, “Who are You, Lord?”
The voice answered Saul.
The voice said, “I am Jesus.”
Jesus said, “You are persecuting Me.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δέ Τίς εἶ Κύριε Ὁ δέ Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις

passages.text: “Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Saul.
Jesus gave Saul a command.
Jesus said, “Get up.”
Jesus said, “Go into the city.”
Jesus said, “Someone will tell you what you must do.”
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ λαληθήσεταί σοι ὅ τί σε δεῖ ποιεῖν

passages.text: The men traveling with Saul stood there speechless. They heard the voice but did not see anyone.
passages.sermon:
Saul traveled with several men.
These men stood still.
They did not speak.
They felt amazed and confused.
They heard a voice.
They did not see anyone.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἄνδρες οἱ συνοδεύοντες αὐτῷ εἱστήκεισαν ἐνεοί ἀκούοντες μὲν τῆς φωνῆς μηδένα δὲ θεωροῦντες

passages.text: Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes he could not see a thing. So they led him by the hand into Damascus.
passages.sermon:
Saul was a man traveling to Damascus.
Saul got up from the ground.
Saul opened his eyes.
Saul could not see anything.
The men with Saul took him by the hand.
They led Saul into Damascus.
passages.original: ἠγέρθη δὲ Σαῦλος ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀνεῳγμένων δὲ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτοῦ οὐδὲν ἔβλεπεν χειραγωγοῦντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἰσήγαγον εἰς Δαμασκόν

passages.text: For three days he was without sight, and he did not eat or drink anything.
passages.sermon: Saul could not see for three days.\r\nHe did not eat during this time.\r\nHe did not drink during this time.
passages.original: καὶ ἦν ἡμέρας τρεῖς μὴ βλέπων καὶ οὐκ ἔφαγεν οὐδὲ ἔπιεν

passages.text: In Damascus there was a disciple named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision, “Ananias!” “Here I am, Lord,” he answered.
passages.sermon:
Ananias was a disciple in Damascus.
The Lord spoke to Ananias in a vision.
The Lord called, “Ananias!”
Ananias answered, “Here I am, Lord.”
passages.original: Ἦν δέ τις μαθητὴς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ὀνόματι Ἁνανίας καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν ὁράματι ὁ Κύριος Ἁνανία Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ Κύριε

passages.text: “Get up!” the Lord told him. “Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, for he is praying.
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to Ananias in a vision.
Ananias was a disciple in Damascus.
The Lord said, “Get up.”
The Lord told Ananias to go to Straight Street.
The Lord told him to go to the house of Judas.
The Lord told him to ask for a man named Saul.
Saul was from Tarsus.
Saul was praying.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν Ἀναστὰς πορεύθητι ἐπὶ τὴν ῥύμην τὴν καλουμένην Εὐθεῖαν καὶ ζήτησον ἐν οἰκίᾳ Ἰούδα Σαῦλον ὀνόματι Ταρσέα ἰδοὺ γὰρ προσεύχεται

passages.text: In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come and place his hands on him to restore his sight.”
passages.sermon:
Saul is a man from Tarsus.
Saul is staying in Damascus.
Saul is praying.
Saul has seen a vision.
In the vision, a man named Ananias comes to him.
Ananias enters the house where Saul is.
Ananias places his hands on Saul.
Ananias does this so that Saul may see again.
passages.original: καὶ εἶδεν ἄνδρα ἐν ὁράματι Ἁνανίαν ὀνόματι εἰσελθόντα καὶ ἐπιθέντα αὐτῷ τὰς χεῖρας ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃ

passages.text: But Ananias answered, “Lord, many people have told me about this man and all the harm he has done to Your saints in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Ananias spoke to the Lord.
He said, “Lord, I have heard about this man from many people.
They told me what he has done.
He has done much harm to Your saints in Jerusalem.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη δὲ Ἁνανίας Κύριε ἤκουσα ἀπὸ πολλῶν περὶ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς τούτου ὅσα κακὰ τοῖς ἁγίοις σου ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: And now he is here with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on Your name.”
passages.sermon:
Saul is here in Damascus.
The chief priests gave Saul authority.
Saul has power to arrest people.
He can arrest everyone who calls on Your name.
passages.original: καὶ ὧδε ἔχει ἐξουσίαν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων δῆσαι πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομά σου

passages.text: “Go!” said the Lord. “This man is My chosen instrument to carry My name before the Gentiles and their kings, and before the people of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to Ananias.
The Lord said, "Go."
Saul is My chosen instrument.
I have chosen Saul to carry My name.
He will speak about Me to the Gentiles.
He will speak about Me to their kings.
He will speak about Me to the people of Israel.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Κύριος Πορεύου ὅτι σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς ἐστίν μοι οὗτος τοῦ βαστάσαι τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐνώπιον τῶν ἐθνῶν τε καὶ βασιλέων υἱῶν τε Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: I will show him how much he must suffer for My name.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke about Saul.
The Lord chose Saul as His servant.
The Lord said, “I will show Saul what he must suffer for My name.”
Saul will experience suffering because he follows Jesus.
Saul will suffer for the sake of Jesus’ name.
passages.original: ἐγὼ γὰρ ὑποδείξω αὐτῷ ὅσα δεῖ αὐτὸν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματός μου παθεῖν

passages.text: So Ananias went to the house, and when he arrived, he placed his hands on Saul. “Brother Saul,” he said, “the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming here, has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
passages.sermon:
Ananias was a disciple in Damascus.
Ananias went to the house where Saul was staying.
Ananias entered the house.
Ananias placed his hands on Saul.
Ananias spoke to Saul.
Ananias said, “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus has sent me.
Jesus appeared to you on the road as you were coming here.
Jesus sent me so that you may see again.
Jesus sent me so that you may be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
passages.original: Ἀπῆλθεν δὲ Ἁνανίας καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν καὶ ἐπιθεὶς ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας εἶπεν Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ ὁ Κύριος ἀπέσταλκέν με Ἰησοῦς ὁ ὀφθείς σοι ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ᾗ ἤρχου ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃς καὶ πλησθῇς Πνεύματος Ἁγίου

passages.text: At that instant, something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and his sight was restored. He got up and was baptized, and after taking some food, he regained his strength. And he spent several days with the disciples in Damascus.
passages.sermon:
Saul was blind.
Suddenly, something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes.
Saul could see again.
Saul stood up.
Saul was baptized.
Saul ate some food.
Saul became strong again.
Saul stayed with the disciples in Damascus for several days.
passages.original: Καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέπεσαν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν ὡς λεπίδες ἀνέβλεψέν τε καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐβαπτίσθη καὶ λαβὼν τροφὴν ἐνίσχυσεν Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐν Δαμασκῷ μαθητῶν ἡμέρας τινὰς

passages.text: Saul promptly began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues, declaring, “He is the Son of God.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was a man who had persecuted Christians.
He had recently met Jesus on the road to Damascus.
He was now in Damascus with the disciples.
Saul went to the synagogues.
He began to speak about Jesus immediately.
He proclaimed Jesus to the people there.
He said, “Jesus is the Son of God.”
passages.original: Καὶ εὐθέως ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ἐκήρυσσεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: All who heard him were astounded and asked, “Isn’t this the man who wreaked havoc in Jerusalem on those who call on this name? And hasn’t he come here to take them as prisoners to the chief priests?”
passages.sermon:
Saul was a man who once persecuted Christians in Jerusalem.
He attacked those who called on the name of Jesus.
He came to Damascus for the same purpose.
He planned to arrest believers and bring them to the chief priests.
Everyone who heard Saul preach was amazed.
They asked, “Isn’t this the man who caused destruction in Jerusalem among those who call on this name?”
They also asked, “Didn’t he come here to capture them and take them to the chief priests as prisoners?”
passages.original: Ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες καὶ ἔλεγον Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ πορθήσας εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομα τοῦτο καὶ ὧδε εἰς τοῦτο ἐληλύθει ἵνα δεδεμένους αὐτοὺς ἀγάγῃ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς

passages.text: But Saul was empowered all the more, and he confounded the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ.
passages.sermon:
Saul was a new Christian.
He became stronger in his faith.
He grew more powerful in his preaching.
Saul lived in Damascus.
He spoke to the Jews who lived there.
He confused the Jews.
He showed them clear proof.
He proved that Jesus is the Christ.
passages.original: Σαῦλος δὲ μᾶλλον ἐνεδυναμοῦτο καὶ συνέχυννεν τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐν Δαμασκῷ συμβιβάζων ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός

passages.text: After many days had passed, the Jews conspired to kill him, but Saul learned of their plot. Day and night they watched the city gates in order to kill him.
passages.sermon:
Saul was a man who preached that Jesus is the Christ.
Many Jews in Damascus heard Saul.
After many days, the Jews made a plan.
They decided to kill Saul.
Saul learned about their plan.
The Jews watched the city gates every day.
They watched the gates every night.
They wanted to find Saul and kill him.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦντο ἡμέραι ἱκαναί συνεβουλεύσαντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν ἐγνώσθη δὲ τῷ Σαύλῳ ἡ ἐπιβουλὴ αὐτῶν παρετηροῦντο δὲ καὶ τὰς πύλας ἡμέρας τε καὶ νυκτὸς ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀνέλωσιν

passages.text: One night, however, his disciples took him and lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall.
passages.sermon:
Saul had disciples in Damascus.
One night, his disciples took him.
They put Saul in a basket.
They lowered Saul through a window in the wall.
They did this to help Saul escape.
passages.original: λαβόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς διὰ τοῦ τείχους καθῆκαν αὐτὸν χαλάσαντες ἐν σπυρίδι

passages.text: When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
passages.sermon:
Saul arrived in Jerusalem.
He tried to join the disciples.
The disciples were all afraid of Saul.
They did not believe that Saul was a disciple.
passages.original: Παραγενόμενος δὲ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐπείραζεν κολλᾶσθαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς καὶ πάντες ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτόν μὴ πιστεύοντες ὅτι ἐστὶν μαθητής

passages.text: Then Barnabas brought him to the apostles and described how Saul had seen the Lord, who spoke to him on the road to Damascus, and how Saul had spoken boldly in that city in the name of Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Barnabas took Saul.
Barnabas brought Saul to the apostles.
Barnabas explained to the apostles what had happened.
Barnabas said Saul saw the Lord on the road to Damascus.
Barnabas said the Lord spoke to Saul.
Barnabas said Saul spoke boldly in Damascus in the name of Jesus.
passages.original: Βαρνάβας δὲ ἐπιλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἤγαγεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους καὶ διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶδεν τὸν Κύριον καὶ ὅτι ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ καὶ πῶς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ἐπαρρησιάσατο ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: So Saul stayed with them, moving about freely in Jerusalem and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Saul was a new disciple of Jesus.
He stayed with the apostles in Jerusalem.
He went in and out among them in the city.
He spoke boldly in the name of the Lord.
passages.original: Καὶ ἦν μετ’ αὐτῶν εἰσπορευόμενος καὶ ἐκπορευόμενος εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ παρρησιαζόμενος ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: He talked and debated with the Grecian Jews, but they tried to kill him.
passages.sermon: Saul spoke with the Grecian Jews.\r\nHe also debated with them.\r\nThe Grecian Jews tried to kill Saul.
passages.original: ἐλάλει τε καὶ συνεζήτει πρὸς τοὺς Ἑλληνιστάς οἱ δὲ ἐπεχείρουν ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν

passages.text: When the brothers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
passages.sermon:
The brothers learned that some people wanted to kill Saul.
The brothers acted quickly.
They took Saul down to Caesarea.
They sent Saul away to Tarsus.
passages.original: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ κατήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάρειαν καὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν αὐτὸν εἰς Ταρσόν

passages.text: Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria experienced a time of peace. It grew in strength and numbers, living in the fear of the Lord and the encouragement of the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon:
The church was in Judea, Galilee, and Samaria.
The church experienced peace.
The church became stronger.
The church grew in numbers.
The church lived in the fear of the Lord.
The church received encouragement from the Holy Spirit.
passages.original: Ἡ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησία καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Γαλιλαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας εἶχεν εἰρήνην οἰκοδομουμένη καὶ πορευομένη τῷ φόβῳ τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ τῇ παρακλήσει τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος ἐπληθύνετο

passages.text: As Peter traveled throughout the area, he went to visit the saints in Lydda.
passages.sermon: Peter was traveling through the whole region.\r\nPeter went to visit the believers who lived in Lydda.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ Πέτρον διερχόμενον διὰ πάντων κατελθεῖν καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἁγίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας Λύδδα

passages.text: There he found a man named Aeneas, who had been paralyzed and bedridden for eight years.
passages.sermon:
Peter visited the believers in Lydda.
He found a man there.
The man’s name was Aeneas.
Aeneas had been paralyzed for eight years.
He lay on his bed all that time.
passages.original: εὗρεν δὲ ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπόν τινα ὀνόματι Αἰνέαν ἐξ ἐτῶν ὀκτὼ κατακείμενον ἐπὶ κραβάττου ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος

passages.text: “Aeneas,” Peter said to him, “Jesus Christ heals you! Get up and put away your mat.” Immediately Aeneas got up, and all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter spoke to Aeneas.
Aeneas was a man who had been paralyzed and bedridden for eight years.
Peter said, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you.”
Peter told Aeneas, “Get up and put away your mat.”
Aeneas immediately got up.
Everyone who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw Aeneas.
They turned to the Lord.
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος Αἰνέα ἰᾶταί σε Ἰησοῦς Χριστός ἀνάστηθι καὶ στρῶσον σεαυτῷ καὶ εὐθέως ἀνέστη καὶ εἶδαν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες Λύδδα καὶ τὸν Σαρῶνα οἵτινες ἐπέστρεψαν ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον

passages.text: In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha (which is translated as Dorcas), who was always occupied with works of kindness and charity.
passages.sermon:
Tabitha lived in Joppa.
She was a disciple.
People also called her Dorcas.
She did many good works.
She often gave to those in need.
She was full of kindness and charity.
passages.original: Ἐν Ἰόππῃ δέ τις ἦν μαθήτρια ὀνόματι Ταβιθά ἣ διερμηνευομένη λέγεται Δορκάς αὕτη ἦν πλήρης ἔργων ἀγαθῶν καὶ ἐλεημοσυνῶν ὧν ἐποίει

passages.text: At that time, however, she became sick and died, and her body was washed and placed in an upper room.
passages.sermon:
Tabitha was a disciple in Joppa.
She was full of good works and acts of charity.
During those days, Tabitha became sick.
She died.
They washed her body.
They placed her body in an upper room.
passages.original: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἀσθενήσασαν αὐτὴν ἀποθανεῖν λούσαντες δὲ ἔθηκαν αὐτὴν ἐν ὑπερῴῳ

passages.text: Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard that Peter was there and sent two men to urge him, “Come to us without delay.”
passages.sermon:
Lydda was a town near Joppa.
Peter was in Lydda.
The disciples in Joppa heard that Peter was in Lydda.
The disciples sent two men to Peter.
The two men urged Peter to come to them quickly.
They said, “Come to us without delay.”
passages.original: ἐγγὺς δὲ οὔσης Λύδδας τῇ Ἰόππῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Πέτρος ἐστὶν ἐν αὐτῇ ἀπέστειλαν δύο ἄνδρας πρὸς αὐτὸν παρακαλοῦντες Μὴ ὀκνήσῃς διελθεῖν ἕως ἡμῶν

passages.text: So Peter got up and went with them. On his arrival, they took him to the upper room. All the widows stood around him, weeping and showing him the tunics and other clothing that Dorcas had made while she was still with them.
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter got up.
Peter went with the two men.
The two men had come from Joppa.
They took Peter to the upper room.
All the widows stood around Peter.
The widows were weeping.
The widows showed Peter the tunics and other clothing.
Dorcas had made these clothes while she was with them.
passages.original: Ἀναστὰς δὲ Πέτρος συνῆλθεν αὐτοῖς ὃν παραγενόμενον ἀνήγαγον εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον καὶ παρέστησαν αὐτῷ πᾶσαι αἱ χῆραι κλαίουσαι καὶ ἐπιδεικνύμεναι χιτῶνας καὶ ἱμάτια ὅσα ἐποίει μετ’ αὐτῶν οὖσα ἡ Δορκάς

passages.text: Then Peter sent them all out of the room. He knelt down and prayed, and turning toward her body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up.
passages.sermon:
Peter was one of Jesus’ apostles.
Peter sent everyone out of the room.
Peter knelt down.
Peter prayed.
Peter turned toward the body of Tabitha.
Peter said, “Tabitha, get up!”
Tabitha opened her eyes.
Tabitha saw Peter.
Tabitha sat up.
passages.original: Ἐκβαλὼν δὲ ἔξω πάντας ὁ Πέτρος καὶ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα προσηύξατο καὶ ἐπιστρέψας πρὸς τὸ σῶμα εἶπεν Ταβιθά ἀνάστηθι ἡ δὲ ἤνοιξεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῆς καὶ ἰδοῦσα τὸν Πέτρον ἀνεκάθισεν

passages.text: Peter took her by the hand and helped her up. Then he called the saints and widows and presented her to them alive.
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter took Dorcas by the hand.
Peter helped Dorcas stand up.
Peter called the believers and the widows.
Peter showed Dorcas to them alive.
passages.original: δοὺς δὲ αὐτῇ χεῖρα ἀνέστησεν αὐτήν φωνήσας δὲ τοὺς ἁγίους καὶ τὰς χήρας παρέστησεν αὐτὴν ζῶσαν

passages.text: This became known all over Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.
passages.sermon: People in Joppa heard about this.\r\nNews spread throughout the whole city.\r\nMany people believed in the Lord.
passages.original: Γνωστὸν δὲ ἐγένετο καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰόππης καὶ ἐπίστευσαν πολλοὶ ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον

passages.text: And Peter stayed for several days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.
passages.sermon: Peter stayed in Joppa for several days.\r\nHe stayed with a man named Simon.\r\nSimon was a tanner.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἡμέρας ἱκανὰς μεῖναι ἐν Ἰόππῃ παρά τινι Σίμωνι βυρσεῖ
